title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization
author: Priya Singh
description: Motivation: reduce wasted compute and latency from padding in continuous batching by grouping requests with similar sequence lengths into buckets and selecting minimal-padding schedules. This PR implements a sequence-length bucketing heuristic, padding-minimization scheduling, and conservative fallbacks for latency-sensitive routes. Design summary: (1) bucketer: online histogram-based bucketing with exponential bucket widths at long tails, cap on bucket count per worker; (2) scheduler: greedy packer that prefers forming batches within the same bucket up to target batch size, but will merge small buckets under high load to preserve throughput; (3) padding minimization: runtime computes per-batch padding cost (tokens * cost_factor) and prioritizes configurations with lowest expected padding overhead subject to latency SLOs; (4) KV cache alignment: ensures KV cache compatibility when merging requests from different model variants/quantizations by checking cache-key signatures; (5) metrics and tracing: added new tags and histograms to track padding waste, bucket distribution, and inter-bucket merge events. Implementation notes: changes are in serving/runtime/batching/{bucketer.py,scheduler.cpp}, serving/runtime/kv_cache/compat.cpp, and a new config surface in serving/runtime/config/batching.yaml. There is a new adaptive throttle that limits bucket fragmentation at low concurrency. Testing and benchmarks included below. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-1421 - [x] unit tests for bucketer and scheduler - [x] integration tests on canary env - [x] metric dashboards updated - [x] rollout plan and kill-switch documented Benchmarks (internal synthetic mix, 8xA100 per worker, mixed seqlen distribution): - median latency: -3.6% (vs current main) - p95 latency: -9.8% (notable improvement on mixed short+long workloads) - throughput (tokens/sec): +14% on average - padding tokens reduced: 22% aggregate - cost/token estimated reduction: ~11% Notes: improvements are strongest on workloads with high variance in sequence length (chat+completion mixes). For heavily short-only workloads, improvements are neutral. Rollout: staged canary -> region rollout -> entire fleet; default sticky off for existing customers, opt-in per-route via batching.strategy=seqlen-bucketing. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains current continuous batching unless enabled. Caveats: when merging across quantization variants, scheduler falls back to conservative batching to avoid cache-miss regressions. Related: ENG-1421 (design), ENG-1599 (kv-cache compatibility investigation).

release_notes: Introduce sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization scheduling to reduce wasted tokens and improve latency on mixed-length workloads. Opt-in per-route via batching.strategy=seqlen-bucketing. See docs/ops/batching-rollout.md for rollout steps and mitigation.
benchmark_summary: On synthetic mixed workload (short+long sequences) measured on 8xA100 workers: p95 latency decreased by 9.8%, throughput increased by 14%, padding tokens reduced by 22%, estimated cost/token down ~11%. Neutral for short-only workloads.
testing_instructions: Unit tests: run pytest serving/runtime/tests::test_bucketer.py serving/runtime/tests::test_scheduler.py. Integration: run scripts/ci/run_benchmark_on_canary.sh against a canary cluster. Manual validation: enable batching.strategy=seqlen-bucketing on a low-traffic route, monitor observability/dashboards/batching_padding and the 'padding_waste' histogram. Watch merged_buckets_count alert.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy to canary (10% of traffic) with feature flag off by default; 2) Run 48h perf + correctness checks, validate padding_waste and p95; 3) Enable for opt-in customers and iterate on bucket configs; 4) Gradually enable by region with kill-switch to revert to legacy batching. Ops runbook in docs/ops/batching-rollout.md.
